subject: maths
title: 2-D and 3-D Shapes: Names, Faces, Edges and Vertices
seo_title: Year 3 2-D and 3-D Shapes Worksheets: Sides, Faces, Edges and Vertices (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Draw 2-D shapes and make 3-D shapes using modelling materials; recognise 3-D shapes in different orientations and describe them.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on 2-D and 3-D shapes: name triangles, pentagons, hexagons and octagons, recognise cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres, pyramids and prisms in any position, count faces, edges and vertices, and make shapes with straws and clay. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Count the sides to name a 2-D shape. Faces, edges and vertices describe a 3-D shape.
key_sub: A shape keeps its name when it is turned. A face is a flat surface, an edge is where two faces meet, and a vertex is a corner. Remember the faces you cannot see.

faq.q: What 2-D and 3-D shapes should a Year 3 child know?
faq.a: 2-D: triangle, square, rectangle, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, circle and semicircle. 3-D: cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere, square-based pyramid and triangular prism.

faq.q: What is the difference between a face, an edge and a vertex?
faq.a: A face is a flat surface, an edge is where two faces meet, and a vertex is a corner where edges meet. A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
“Diamond” is not a maths name. A square turned on its corner is still a square. A shape with 4 equal sides but no right angles is a rhombus.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn 3-D shapes at home?
faq.a: Look for shapes around the house, such as a tin of beans (cylinder) or a cereal box (cuboid), and count the faces, edges and vertices together. Making shapes with straws and modelling clay helps too.

items.q: Name this 2-D shape.
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 right angles. The long sides are longer than the short sides, so it is a rectangle, not a square. Turning a shape or making it bigger or smaller does not change its name.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 vertices, so it is a triangle. It is upside down, but it is still a triangle.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: Count the sides: 5 straight sides make a pentagon. The sides do not have to be equal.

items.q: Name this 2-D shape.
items.e: Count the sides: 5 straight sides make a pentagon.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Count each vertex once. Put a finger on one vertex and go round until you are back where you started: 8 vertices. The shape has the same number of sides and vertices.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 vertices, so it is a triangle. A long, thin triangle is still a triangle.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Count each side once. Put a finger on one side and go round until you are back where you started: 6 sides. The shape has the same number of sides and vertices.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Count each vertex once. Put a finger on one vertex and go round until you are back where you started: 5 vertices. The shape has the same number of sides and vertices.
A semicircle has 1 straight side (along the bottom) and 1 curved side.

items.q: Which shape is a hexagon?
items.e: B has 6 sides, so it is a hexagon. The others have 5, 8 and 4 sides. A hexagon does not need equal sides.

items.q: Which shape is a square?
items.e: D has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. It is a square that has been turned. The other diamond shape has equal sides but no right angles, so it is not a square.

items.q: Name this 2-D shape.
items.e: Count the sides: 6 straight sides make a hexagon. The sides do not have to be equal.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: Count the sides: 6 straight sides make a hexagon.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: Count the sides: 8 straight sides make an octagon. Count the short sides at the corners too.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It is flat and perfectly round, so it is a circle. A sphere is a 3-D shape, like a ball.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: Count the sides: 8 straight sides make an octagon.
It is half of a circle: 1 curved side and 1 straight side. It is a semicircle.

items.q: A 2-D shape has 6 straight sides. What is it called?
items.e: 6 sides: hexagon. 5 sides: pentagon. 8 sides: octagon.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles, so it is a square. It is only turned. “Diamond” is not the maths name.

items.q: How many vertices does a pentagon have?
items.e: A pentagon has 5 sides and 5 vertices (corners). A shape with straight sides has the same number of sides and vertices.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.
It has 2 circle faces at the ends and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cylinder.

items.q: Both pictures show the same 3-D shape in different positions. What is it?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. Turning a shape does not change its name.
It is round all over, like a ball, so it is a sphere. A circle is a flat 2-D shape.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It is turned so you see a triangle end at the front. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.
It has 2 circle faces at the ends and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. Turning a shape does not change its name.
It has 1 circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone. It is upside down, but it is still a cone.
C is a cone: it has 1 circle face and comes to a point. It is lying on its side.
It has 1 circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone.
D is a triangular prism: it has 2 triangle faces joined by rectangles. It is standing on a triangle.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has a square face at the bottom and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid. It is turned, but it is still a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It is standing on a triangle face, but it is still a triangular prism. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has a square face at the bottom and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube.
It has 2 circle faces at the ends and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder.
A is a cuboid: it has 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares. It is standing on its end.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cube.
It has 1 circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cone.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid. It is standing on its end, but it is still a cuboid.

items.q: This is a cube. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Do not forget the vertex at the top.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some faces are at the back. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some faces are at the back. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: Zara counts 12 on a cuboid. She counted correctly. What did she count?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. So 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: A flat surface of a 3-D shape is called a …
items.e: A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices?
items.e: A sphere is round all over, like a ball. It has only one curved surface.

items.q: The line where two faces of a 3-D shape meet is called an …
items.e: Where two faces meet there is an edge.

items.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
items.e: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces, one at each end, and a curved surface.

items.q: This is a cuboid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: Leo says a cube has 8 edges. He is wrong. What did he count?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices (corners) and 12 edges. Leo counted the vertices.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 5 vertices?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 4 vertices round the square and 1 at the top: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: How many vertices does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 8 vertices: 4 at the top and 4 at the bottom. 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: How many flat faces does a cone have?
items.e: A cone has 1 flat circle face. The rest is a curved surface that comes to a point.

items.q: A corner of a 3-D shape, where edges meet, is called a …
items.e: A corner is a vertex. More than one vertex are called vertices.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

sets.title: Faces of 3-D shapes and making models

items.q: This model is made from straws and balls of clay. Which 3-D shape is it?
items.e: It has 12 straws (edges) and 8 balls of clay (vertices). All the edges are the same length, so it is a cube.

items.q: Lily prints with the bottom face of a square-based pyramid. What shape does she print?
items.e: The base of a square-based pyramid is a square, so it prints a square. The other faces would print triangles.

items.q: How many square faces does a cube have?
items.e: A cube has 6 square faces. You can see 3 of them; 3 more are at the back and underneath.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 1 circle face and comes to a point?
items.e: A cone has 1 circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point. A pyramid also has a point, but its base is a square.

items.q: You make a cube from straws and balls of clay. How many straws do you need?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges, so you need 12 straws. 8 is the number of vertices (balls of clay). Each straw makes an edge and each ball of clay makes a vertex.

items.q: Which 2-D shapes are the faces of a triangular prism?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle at each end (2 triangles) and 3 rectangles joining them: 5 faces.

items.q: How many straws do you need to make a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 8 edges: 4 round the square and 4 going up to the top. Each straw makes an edge and each ball of clay makes a vertex.

items.q: Which 3-D shape can you NOT make from straight straws and balls of clay?
items.e: A sphere is curved all over and has no edges or vertices, so straight straws cannot make it.

items.q: This model is made from straws and balls of clay. Which 3-D shape is it?
items.e: It has 9 straws (edges) and 6 balls of clay (vertices). It has 2 triangles at the ends joined by 3 straws, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: This model is made from straws and balls of clay. Which 3-D shape is it?
items.e: It has 8 straws (edges) and 5 balls of clay (vertices). It has a square at the bottom and 4 straws going up to one point, so it is a square-based pyramid.
Each end of a cylinder is a flat circle. It looks like an oval in the picture because we see it from the side.

items.q: Which 2-D shapes are the faces of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square at the bottom and 4 triangles that meet at the top: 5 faces.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has some triangle faces?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 4 triangle faces. Cubes and cuboids have squares and rectangles, and a cylinder has circles.

items.q: You make a cube from straws and balls of clay. How many balls of clay do you need?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices, so you need 8 balls of clay: 4 at the top and 4 at the bottom. Each straw makes an edge and each ball of clay makes a vertex.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 2 circle faces and a curved surface?
items.e: A cylinder has 2 circle faces (one at each end) and a curved surface. A cone has only 1 circle face.

items.q: Charlie dips the end of a cylinder in paint. Then he presses it on paper. What shape does he print?
items.e: The end of a cylinder is a flat circle face, so it prints a circle. A print is always a flat 2-D shape.

items.q: Which 3-D shape can roll?
items.e: A cylinder has a curved surface, so it can roll. Shapes with only flat faces slide but do not roll.

items.q: Amelia has 6 balls of clay and 9 straws. She uses them all to make one 3-D shape. Which shape?
items.e: 6 vertices and 9 edges: that is a triangular prism. A square-based pyramid has 5 vertices and 8 edges.

items.q: You make a triangular prism from straws and balls of clay. What do you need?
items.e: A triangular prism has 9 edges (3 on each triangle and 3 joining them) and 6 vertices. Each straw makes an edge and each ball of clay makes a vertex.
The flat face at the bottom of a cone is a circle. The cone looks like a triangle from the side, but it has no triangle faces.

sets.title: Shapes all around us: word problems

items.q: Ethan puts a sticker on every face of 3 dice. How many stickers does he use?
items.e: A dice is a cube with 6 faces. 3 dice: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 stickers. 24 uses the vertices and 36 uses the edges.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a dice?
items.e: A dice has 6 square faces that are all the same size, so it is a cube.

items.q: Harry cuts a circle in half with one straight cut through the middle. What shape is each piece?
items.e: Half of a circle is a semicircle. It has 1 curved side and 1 straight side.

items.q: Zara has 20 straws. She makes one cube. How many straws are left?
items.e: A cube uses 12 straws (12 edges). 20 − 12 = 8 straws left. 14 comes from taking away 6 faces instead of 12 edges.

items.q: Ruby uses 6 lolly sticks to make a closed 2-D shape. Each stick is one side. What shape does she make?
items.e: 6 sides make a hexagon.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a long chocolate box with a triangle at each end?
items.e: 2 triangle ends joined by 3 rectangles make a triangular prism.

items.q: Jack holds a 3-D shape with 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Not all of its faces are squares. What shape is it?
items.e: Cubes and cuboids both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. All the faces of a cube are squares, so this is a cuboid.

items.q: Grace counts all the vertices on 2 square-based pyramids. How many vertices are there?
items.e: Each pyramid has 5 vertices: 4 round the square and 1 at the top. 5 + 5 = 10. 8 forgets the top vertices.

items.q: Evie has a cube, a cylinder, a sphere, a cone and a cuboid. How many of them have a curved surface?
items.e: The cylinder, the sphere and the cone have curved surfaces: 3 shapes. The cube and cuboid have only flat faces.

items.q: A STOP road sign is an octagon. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: An octagon has 8 sides and 8 vertices.

items.q: Maya draws a 2-D shape with 8 straight sides. What is it called?
items.e: 8 sides make an octagon. 6 sides make a hexagon.

items.q: A tin of beans has a paper label all the way round. Which part of the tin does the label cover?
items.e: The label goes round the side of the tin. That is the curved surface of the cylinder. The 2 flat faces are the top and bottom.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a tin of beans?
items.e: A tin has 2 circle ends and a curved side, so it is a cylinder.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a cereal box?
items.e: A cereal box has 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: George makes a triangular prism and a square-based pyramid. He puts a ball of clay at every vertex. How many balls does he use?
items.e: A triangular prism has 6 vertices and a square-based pyramid has 5. 6 + 5 = 11. 17 adds the edges (9 + 8).

items.q: Poppy makes 2 cubes from straws. How many straws does she use?
items.e: 1 cube needs 12 straws (12 edges). 2 cubes: 12 + 12 = 24 straws. 16 uses the vertices (8 + 8).

items.q: Mohammed cuts out 3 triangles and 2 squares from card. How many vertices do they have altogether?
items.e: 3 triangles: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. 2 squares: 4 + 4 = 8. 9 + 8 = 17 vertices. 5 counts the shapes, not the vertices.

items.q: What 3-D shape is an Egyptian pyramid with a square base?
items.e: It has a square base and 4 triangle faces that meet at the top, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What 3-D shape is a football?
items.e: A football is round all over, so it is a sphere. A circle is flat.

items.q: What 3-D shape is an ice-cream cone?
items.e: It has a circle at the top, a curved side and a point at the bottom, so it is a cone.
